intro.heading: One Control Set, Many Frameworks
paragraphs: Compliance rarely arrives one framework at a time. A payments partner asks for PCI DSS 4.0, a US enterprise buyer wants a SOC 2 Type II report, your regulator expects controls aligned to its cyber security directions, and somewhere in the middle a healthcare client raises HIPAA. Treated as four separate projects, each one repeats the same work: the same access reviews, the same change records, the same vendor assessments, collected four times by four different people.

We run compliance as a single programme. Your obligations are mapped onto one control set, so a documented quarterly access review satisfies the SOC 2 logical access criteria, the PCI DSS requirement for least privilege and the corresponding NIST CSF 2.0 outcome at the same time. Where frameworks genuinely diverge, and they do, we scope the difference explicitly rather than pretending a generic policy covers it.

Be clear about what we are and are not. Arysec does the readiness work: scoping, control design, internal testing, evidence assembly and sitting beside you through fieldwork. The opinion itself always comes from an independent firm, because the rules that give an attestation its value stop whoever designed your controls from also testing them for the report. We treat that split as a discipline rather than a limitation, since it forces our internal testing to be harder than the assessor's. Obligations for entities supervised by the Reserve Bank of India, SEBI or IRDAI are revised periodically and differ by licence class, so your compliance counsel should confirm where yours leaves you.

items.title: SOC 2 Readiness
items.description: We scope the Trust Services Criteria that apply, design controls for Type I, then run the observation window with monitored evidence collection so your Type II period does not fail on a missed sample.

items.title: PCI DSS 4.0 Scoping
items.description: Cardholder data flows are traced end to end, assessment scope is reduced where segmentation or tokenisation allows, and each requirement is tested against the defined approach or a documented customised implementation.

items.title: NIST CSF 2.0 Maturity
items.description: Current and target profiles are scored across all six functions, including Govern, giving your board a maturity view that is comparable year on year and maps cleanly onto other frameworks.

items.title: Indian Regulatory Alignment
items.description: Regulated entities under the Reserve Bank of India, SEBI or IRDAI face sector-specific cyber security and outsourcing expectations. We read the directions that apply to your licence class and align controls, reporting and testing accordingly.

items.title: Gap Analysis and Remediation
items.description: Every control is assessed twice: is it designed to meet the requirement, and is it operating as designed. Findings are rated by audit risk and issued with owners, effort estimates and target dates.

items.title: Evidence and Auditor Liaison
items.description: Evidence requests are answered from a maintained repository rather than assembled under pressure. We manage the assessor's sample requests, walkthrough scheduling and follow-up questions, and we push back where a request exceeds agreed scope.

deliverables.heading: Artefacts You Keep

process.title: Boundary
process.description: We establish which frameworks genuinely apply, then draw the boundary: which entities, systems, data flows and third parties are in. Getting this wrong is the most common cause of audit overruns.

process.title: Gap Register
process.description: Interviews, configuration review, document inspection and sample testing produce a rated gap register. You learn early which findings are quick policy fixes and which need engineering time or budget approval.

process.title: Close Out
process.description: Your team closes findings with our support: control design, policy drafting, tooling configuration and evidence workflows. We retest each item and hold a formal readiness review before you engage the external assessor.

process.title: Fieldwork
process.description: We sit alongside you through fieldwork, managing sample requests and walkthroughs, then set the recurring calendar of access reviews, risk assessments and vendor checks that keeps the next cycle shorter.

benefits.title: No Surprises at Fieldwork

faqs.question: Can Arysec issue our SOC 2 report or PCI DSS certificate?
faqs.answer: We do not, and no consultancy honestly can. A SOC 2 attestation is issued by an independent licensed CPA firm, a PCI DSS Report on Compliance by a qualified assessor, and an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate by an accredited certification body. Independence rules prevent the same firm from building your controls and then attesting to them. We do the readiness work, run internal testing and support you through fieldwork; you appoint the assessor directly.

faqs.question: What is a realistic timeline for a first SOC 2 Type II?
faqs.answer: Plan for six to twelve months. Readiness and remediation typically run three to six months depending on how much control design already exists, then the Type II observation window needs a minimum of three months of operating evidence, and most buyers expect six or twelve. Type I can be reached sooner and is a reasonable interim answer for a prospect, but few enterprise procurement teams accept it as a permanent substitute.

faqs.question: Between our internal audit function and our GRC tool, what is left for you to add?
faqs.answer: Usually scope interpretation and testing depth. Internal audit knows your business; it rarely knows how a particular assessor reads PCI DSS requirement 11, or which SOC 2 samples get rejected. A GRC tool stores evidence, it does not decide whether that evidence proves operating effectiveness. We work alongside both, configure the tool against the mapped control set, and train your team to run the cycle without us.

faqs.question: How much of this lands on our engineering team?
faqs.answer: More than vendors like to admit, and we would rather say so up front. Policy drafting, control mapping, testing and evidence structuring are ours. Changing an access model, enabling log retention, segmenting a network or fixing a deployment pipeline is engineering work only your team can do. We reduce the load by sequencing findings so one change satisfies several requirements, and by writing tickets with enough technical detail to be picked up without a meeting.

faqs.question: Does being compliant with these frameworks mean we are secure?
faqs.answer: No. A framework is a floor agreed by committee, and an assessor tests a sample at a point in time. PCI DSS will not stop a phishing-led account takeover, and clean attestation reports have been issued to organisations that were later breached. We use the compliance programme as the vehicle for controls that also reduce real risk, and we tell you plainly where a requirement is a paperwork obligation rather than a security improvement.
